newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa names four Telkom candidates.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa names four Telkom candidates.

text.p: South African Minister for Posts and Telecommunications Jay Naidoo on Monday named Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom, Telekom Malaysia and South Western Bell as finalists for a 20 to 30 percent stake in the state-owned Telkom utility.
Ministry spokesman Connie Malusi said Naidoo would prefer that the four candidates would pare off into two consortia for the next stage that begins early in December with a request for proposals.
"The Ministry remains confident that the strategic equity partner (ep) process will reach a successful conclusion on time by the end of March next year," Malusi told Reuters.
The Ministry has previously said the sale of the stake is expected to raise some five to six billion rand ($1.1-1.3 billion).
Last month Naidoo shortlisted seven candidates for the Telkom stake. KPN, Stet and Telia of Sweden are not included in the latest shortlist.
The Ministry has reserved a further 10 percent stake in Telkom for black business and for communities disadvantaged under apartheid.

Naidoo said in a statement he held a workshop on Sunday with representatives of labour, black business and disadvantaged communities "to discuss the best way to use the 10 percent Telkom stake to achieve genuine and lasting black empowerment in the telecommunications sector."
Naidoo said the workshop agreed that the process should include black involvement in the management and control of Telkom in the long term.
Three task teams had been formed to develop ideas on skills promotion, equity participation and entrepreneurial development.

Malusi said the negotiations with the foreign candidates would take into account their financial bid, as well as their potential contribution to technology, management expertise and human resource development at Telkom.

The Ministry has previously said Telkom needs 30 billion rand in the next five years to double the number of telephone lines from four million serving mainly white areas at present to eight million, with a much greter penetration of traditionally black areas.
Half of that amount is expected to come from Telkom's own revenue with the balance from borrowings and cash from the strategic equity partner.
The sale of a stake in Telkom to foreign bidders is the first major step in the South African government's privatisation programme and is seen as a litmus test of its commitment to economic reform.
